_purpose: Reviewed answers to one question about the committed equity bars (`series` in data/weekly): is each the bar of the session its file names, as scripts/audit_series.py found. An entry is a statement that the bar was looked at, not that it was fixed: the files are observations and are never edited (DATA_FEED.md sec.1). 'committed' is what the file holds, 'session' is the session the bar actually is where the audit could tell, 'provider' is the provider's bar for the named session put on the file's adjustment basis, and 'origin' says who wrote the bar: slice_week with the file (backfill), slice_week into an existing week (merged), or the Friday job (live).
_regenerate: python scripts/audit_series.py --write   (replaces 'audited' and 'findings', keeps everything else, and carries a finding's cause forward only while the finding is unchanged; review what is NEW first and give it a cause here by hand)
_method: A committed close is an adjusted close as of its fetch date, so it is expected to differ from a fresh fetch for any name that has paid a dividend or split since; level against level proves nothing. Two things do not move. Volume is never dividend-adjusted: the committed volume is one session's volume, times any split since. And the committed close over today's adjusted close for the same session is one factor per ticker and fetch date, which the provider states itself as Adj Close / Close on the fetch date. A session that fits both is the bar. The close alone decides only when the volume fits no session at all, restated since or not final when read: 'close_alone' counts those, and 'tied' the ones among them whose close is also another session's of the same week, where nothing says which of the two bars it is. 'audited.weekly.reach' is what the audit could have found: for every bar that passed, the session before it is put in its place and asked about. 'tried' is how many ok bars have such a session, 'named' how often it is named, 'blind_on_close' how many the close alone would pass because the close did not change. 'no_volume' lists every committed bar with a volume of 0 or null, whatever its class. 'carried' lists findings kept from the previous list because the provider did not answer for them on the day of this run.

_classes.prior_session: the named session has a bar at the provider and the committed bar is an earlier session of the same week
_classes.stand_in: the ticker did not trade on the named session; the committed bar is an earlier session of the week and the file does not say so
_classes.other_session: the bar of a session the file does not name and that is not earlier in its week: a later day of it, or a day just outside it
_classes.differs: no session's close on the file's adjustment basis: restated since, or read before the session was final. 'session' is set only where the volume still names one
_classes.conflict: close and volume name different sessions; no session is given, the witnesses say which each names
_classes.unverified: the provider has no bar for the ticker in the file's week, or did not answer; never an ok

delisted_midweek.what: 2026-08-07.json holds EA's close of Tuesday 2026-08-04, its last session, under Friday's date, on no volume and with no mark.
delisted_midweek.evidence: The file has EA at 209.70 on volume 0. The provider keeps one EA bar: 2026-08-04, 209.70 on 48,430,629 shares, and nothing after it. EA was taken private at 210 a share (wiki/communication-services.md) and delisted that day (wiki/universe.md). The two files before this one list EA in missing ('no bar for week of ...'), so by 2026-08-12 the provider's EA history already had a hole from 2026-07-20 to 07-31. slice_week took the last EA row dated on or before the Friday and kept its close without its date. Whether that row was the 08-04 bar before its volume was posted, or a later print carrying 209.70 forward on no trades (wiki/communication-services.md of 2026-08-22 records the quote going dark after an 8/10 bar), the file cannot say and the provider no longer has the row. Either way it is not a Friday close: EA had no session on 2026-08-07. Identified by the close alone; the committed volume is not that bar's.
delisted_midweek.resolution: Panel left as written; not corrected, because no sign-off was asked for it. Nothing in this repo or in sector-regime-heatmap reads the bar: EA is not one of the sixteen ETFs market_state derives from, was never in the focus set, and no Council, Arena or portfolio book held it. If it is to go, the AVB 2026-08-21 correction is the pattern: a 2026-08-07.corrected.json that moves EA to missing with 'zero-volume' in the reason, which rebuild_corrections.py already re-applies. The writer is the open item: slice_week still takes the last bar on or before the Friday, and truth_check --feed accepts a close behind volume 0.

dead_symbol_no_record.what: The provider no longer has the week, and nothing else on record covers it.
dead_symbol_no_record.evidence: EA was delisted 2026-08-04; AVB was merged into EQR, now VMRK, after 2026-08-14. Of a delisted symbol the provider keeps its last bar and nothing else (EA 2026-08-04, AVB 2026-08-14), and asked in a batch it sometimes returns not even that. These 155 bars, AVB 2024-08-16 to 2025-08-22 and EA 2024-08-16 to 2026-07-17, were cut by slice_week from the download of 2026-08-12 and each has a volume. That is all that can be said for them. The 29,891 other bars from that download that can still be checked are every one the session their file names, which is a reason to expect these are too and is not a check of them.
dead_symbol_no_record.resolution: Left unverified: not ok, and not a finding of a wrong session. Neither name is read by anything today. AVB was in the heatmap's Real Estate basket until 2026-09-21 and no run scored it: the 2026-08-21 run had AVB dropped at its end week by the correction, and every later end week lists it in missing.

dead_symbol_spreadsheet_agrees.what: The provider no longer has the week; the owner's spreadsheet has, and agrees with the file session by session.
dead_symbol_spreadsheet_agrees.evidence: Watchlist_110_Weekly_History_1Year.xlsx (written 2026-08-24; price-only closes, one row per week dated with the session it is from; BACKFILL_44.md) carries AVB from 2025-08-29. For each of these 50 files its AVB row is dated the session the file names: the Friday, and the Thursday for the three holiday files (2026-04-02, 06-18, 07-02). Volume agrees in all 50 (48 to within 100 shares, the other two to 0.03 percent), and committed close over spreadsheet close is one constant per dividend quarter, 0.961800, 0.970575, 0.979844, 0.990760 and 1.000000, each steady to 6e-7 and stepping at AVB's four ex-dates. A bar from another session would break both. Checked by hand on 2026-10-05; the spreadsheet is not in the repo and the script does not read it.
dead_symbol_spreadsheet_agrees.resolution: Unverified in the script's terms, because the provider is its only witness; on the evidence above they are the named session's bars. Listed apart from the 155 so the difference is on record.

print_behind_no_volume_corrected.what: The AVB print behind zero volume that 2026-08-21.corrected.json already drops.
print_behind_no_volume_corrected.evidence: 65.9005 on volume 0, a week after AVB's last bar. It is that bar restated: 184.06 on 2026-08-14 divided by 2.793, the merger ratio, which the provider records against AVB as a split. A week-old close on a new share basis, printed under 2026-08-21 with no trade behind it. Known since 2026-08-22 (CLAUDE.md, Known data defects); listed because the audit meets it in the base file.
print_behind_no_volume_corrected.resolution: Corrected before this audit: 2026-08-21.corrected.json lists AVB in missing and readers prefer it. The base file is unchanged.

weekly_bar_fallback.what: AVB in the 2026-08-28 file is the week's last print, taken from a weekly bar: 68.14 from Monday 2026-08-24, a week after AVB stopped trading, and it is the successor company's price.
weekly_bar_fallback.evidence: The file was not written by snapshot.fetch_weekly_bars. Its missing reasons read 'no usable close for 2026-08-28 (daily NaN + weekly unavailable)', a text no writer in this repo produces: on Saturday 2026-08-29 the provider's daily closes for the Friday were all null, and the runner's one-off script took every close from the provider's 1wk bar and the volume from the daily row (feed_run_2026-08-28/step3_weekly_v2.py and that day's log, on the runner; neither is in the repo). For the 330 names that traded on the Friday the 1wk close is the Friday close, and the audit confirms each against the daily bar. AVB had no Friday row, so it got the 1wk close and a null volume. data/daily/2026-08-24.json holds the same 68.14 for AVB dated the Monday, and 68.14 is VMRK's close that day (VMRK closed the Friday at 65.54): the provider was printing the successor's price under the dead symbol. It is the same Saturday whose index closes were Thursday's (macro/instrument_audit.json, index_bar_absent_at_fetch).
weekly_bar_fallback.resolution: Not corrected: no sign-off was asked, and a live file is outside what this audit was asked to cover. The correction of 2026-10-05 for the three instrument closes is a full copy and carries the bar too. Dropping it needs a change first: rebuild_corrections.py recognises a dropped bar by volume 0 in the base, and this one's volume is null. No scored output used it. The heatmap's only run to open the 2026-08-28 file was 2026-09-25, as its month-start week, after AVB had left the watchlist. A reader that did score AVB from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-28 would get -63.3 percent, and the heatmap's zero-volume guard would not stop it, because null is not 0.

evening_read.what: A close read on the evening of the session, half a cent under the one the provider settled on.
evening_read.evidence: 2026-09-25.json was fetched at 22:14 UTC, 18:14 ET, on the Friday. COST 922.765, NFLX 71.145 and ORLY 86.115 against 922.77, 71.15 and 86.12 now; the file's other 331 closes are the provider's. None of its 334 volumes is: 325 are short of the final count, by up to 32 percent. (BTC and GLD, merged into the file on 2026-10-06 from a later fetch, are not among the 334.) The file read on a Saturday at 13:07 UTC, 2026-10-02.json, matches the provider in every close and every volume.
evening_read.resolution: Panel left as written: half a cent on three closes, 0.7 bp at most, and no return changes sign (COST and NFLX are in the focus set; their week returns move by under 0.01 point). The weekly job now runs on Saturday after 13:00 UTC for the futures' sake (DATA_FEED.md sec.1b), which is late enough for these as well.
